newsitem.title: BELARUS: Ukraine's Kuchma notes worsening Russian relations.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma notes worsening Russian relations.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma sealed stronger economic links with Belarus on Friday and said relations with Russia were deteriorating.
Kuchma met pro-Russian President Alexander Lukashenko near the two countries' borders and signed a communique aimed among other things at simplifying customs rules.
But Kuchma said he was unhappy with the state of relations between Kiev and the third Slav state, Russia.

"I cannot fail to notice a systematic deterioration in Ukrainian-Russian relations recently. Investigations are useless, we need concrete steps by Russia and Ukraine to eradicate the problems," he said.
Lukashenko was elected partly on promises of forming some kind of union with Russia.

On Friday, the two leaders said they had signed more documents than expected and they agreed to open more border crossing points. But the Ukrainian leader stressed: "There are and will be two states".
"If we fulfil what we agreed today, we will in reality move so far forward that our relations will overtake all relations Belarus has with other states," Lukashenko said.
Ukraine's relations with Russia are strained by failure to agree on how to divide the former Soviet Black Sea Fleet.

They were aggravated further on Tuesday when the Ukrainian newspaper Vseukrainskiye Vedomosti published the text and a photograph of what it said was a letter from Russian deputy foreign minister Sergei Krylov to President Boris Yeltsin's chief foreign policy adviser, Dmitry Ryurikov.
The Russian foreign ministry said the letter, in which Kuchma's policy was described as "anti-Russian and destructive," was a fake, and Krylov denied he wrote it.
Kuchma declined to comment on the letter itself but made clear he was unhappy with relations with Moscow.

Ukraine and Russia have failed to sign a friendship treaty since the Soviet Union broke up in 1991 and Yeltsin had vowed to make Ukraine his first port of call after recovering from the heart problems which dogged him last year.
Kuchma is due this month to attend a summit in Moscow of the leaders of the 12 former Soviet republics which make up the loose Commonwealth of Independent States.
He is expected to hold separate talks with Yeltsin if the Russian president, who has pneumonia, is well enough.
